name: SEARCH
description: SEARCH returns the position of one text string inside another. It is case-insensitive and supports wildcards.
tldr: Finds the position of text within another text string, case-insensitive.

parameters.name: find_text
parameters.description: The text to find. Supports wildcards * and ?.

parameters.name: start_num
parameters.description: The character position to start searching from (default 1).

basicExample.description: Find the position of text regardless of case
basicExample.explanation: SEARCH is case-insensitive, so it finds "abc" at position 1.

advancedExamples.title: Wildcard search
advancedExamples.description: Find any three-digit number in a code
advancedExamples.explanation: The first three-character sequence appears at position 5.

howItWorks: SEARCH scans within_text for find_text and returns the position of the first match. It is case-insensitive and allows * and ? wildcards. If not found, it returns #VALUE!.

howToSteps.name: Enter text to find
howToSteps.text: Type the substring, optionally using wildcards.

howToSteps.name: Enter text to search
howToSteps.text: Type the cell or string containing the text.

howToSteps.name: Optional start position
howToSteps.text: Add a start number to skip earlier characters.

limitations: Case-insensitive only; cannot force case-sensitive matching.
Returns #VALUE! if the text is not found.
Wildcard ? matches any single character; * matches any sequence.

commonErrors.fix: Use IFERROR to handle missing text.
Adjust the pattern or use FIND for literal matching.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: SEARCH works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: What is the difference between SEARCH and FIND?
faq.answer: SEARCH is case-insensitive and supports wildcards. FIND is case-sensitive and does not support wildcards.

faq.question: Can SEARCH use regular expressions?
faq.answer: No. In Google Sheets, use REGEXMATCH for regex search.

faq.question: How do I search for a literal * or ??
faq.answer: Use a tilde (~) before the wildcard: SEARCH("~*", A2).
